newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel after the plunge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel after the plunge.

text.p: Intel Corp options continued to see heavy traffic, even though the overall market regained calm for now after Friday's rollercoaster ride triggered by Intel stock's plunge, traders said.

While call speculators' bottom-fishing in popular technology stocks has often proved fruitless, traders were unsure about Intel, a dominant microprocessor maker that has so often led the stock market's bounce after pullbacks.
"There is still a very strong buy-on-the-dip mentality on the street," said Bob Dickey, a managing director of Dain Bosworth.
Intel's June calls on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) had volume of more than 4,400 contracts in the 155, 160 and the 165 strike prices.
The stock was off 1-3/4 at 149-3/4 shortly before the close. On Friday, it had fallen to an intrday low of 140 and closed more than 12 full points lower at 151-1/2.

While some of the deeper out-of-the-money calls saw long liquidation today, Rod Jamieson, vice president of options strategy at EVEREN Securities, said most of the retail activity seemed to be call buying.

Puts also had good volume, particularly in the 150 strike, which had traded more than 7,500 contracts. Hedging demand was strong because Intel has been a very popular stock among institutional investors, traders said.
Dickey said Intel stock did not look so bad technically.
"This still qualifies as a very normal pullback in a longer-term uptrend," he said, adding that the trend would be intact as long as the stock did not go below 140.
But he warned that call options might not be an appropriate vehicle right now, even for the bullish.
He said implied volatility levels had become very plump after last week's turmoil and it usually took time for a stock to recover after a sharp decline.

"I think call buyers have to be a little nimble, a little more than they're used to being on this stock, because it's going to take the stock some time to regroup," he said. "I think time is going to be their enemy in the next few weeks."

Implied volatilities for most out-of-the-money strikes for June options, both puts and calls, were slightly above 40 percent, compared with the stock's historical one-month volatility in the low-30 percent area.
Elsewhere, activity was slow and the busier issues appeared to be of more institutional nature.
Washington Mutual Inc July 60 calls and puts traded 3,800 and 3,700 contracts respectively.
Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer and Co, said it looked like a conversion-type strategy against a short stock position. The stock was off 5/8 at 55.

Washington Mutual and Great Western Financial Corp agreed to a merger in March, and a judge was to rule shortly on a request by a hostile bidder for Great Western to delay a June 13 vote by Great Western shareholders on the merger plan.
